summary: NC.6 is a process endpoint whose listed outputs belong to NC.1–NC.5 and EffectiveDiophantineMethods ED.6. This checkpoint completes its ownership and dependency screen and proposes removing the stage, preserving the existing NC.5 to ED.6 edge. It introduces no mathematical nodes. Coverage remains partial because no accepted restructuring result drops NC.6; source-scoped reconstruction, finite local loci and certified global enumeration retain separate hypotheses and owners.

gaps.title: NC.6 removal awaits accepted restructuring
gaps.detail: PROTOCOL §15 permits node-free closed coverage only for a layer dropped by an accepted restructuring. At this checkpoint, no research/blueprint/restructure/RS-*.result.json records an accepted NC.6 drop. Its parent packet still explicitly leaves removal pending acceptance. Adding a process node or duplicating NC.1–NC.5 mathematics would violate the issue. The permitted deliverables can make the proposal reviewable but cannot record the external acceptance or change the atlas. This is a structural blocker, not a new mathematical gap in the supplier layers.

sourceIssues.locator: Published Lemma 4.7, p.1136; same tail condition in arXiv:2101.01862v4, p.25.
sourceIssues.printed: The truncation index is constrained only at coefficient indices satisfying ord_p(F_i) + i = n.
sourceIssues.correction: For all i ≥ m require ord_p(F_i) + i ≥ n, using ord_p(0) = infinity; retain the convergence and multiplicity obligations of the ED.6 root-determination-precision node.
sourceIssues.reason: The coefficient of T^i in G(T) = p^(−k)F(pT) has valuation ord_p(F_i) + i − k. A polynomial truncation of degree below m modulo p^(n−k) therefore needs a bound for every tail index. For F(x) = p^5 − p x + x^2, m = 2, n = 5, k = 2, the only equality index is 0, whereas G(T) = p^3 − T + T^2 has a unit coefficient in degree 2. This repeats the obstruction already recorded by the ED supplier; it supplies no new root-isolation proof.
sourceIssues.known: Already recorded as EffectiveDiophantineMethods/E21, confirmed by REV-EffectiveDiophantineMethods~3. Freshly checked here in the published and v4 passages; not claimed new.

frontiers: Mochizuki's closed-curve Isom theorem is not the section conjecture and supplies no rational-point enumeration algorithm. Hom claims and variants for other bases require their own NC.1 sources.

A finite-level locus contains the specified global rational or integral points through the local/global diagram. Finiteness under verified dimension or quadratic-height hypotheses is distinct from equality with the global set.

Eventual equality in BDCKW §3.1 uses that source's minimal Z-model and stringent local conditions. Do not generalize it to arbitrary number fields or identify it with Kim 2009 Conjecture 1's dimension inequality.

Any unresolved Bloch–Kato, Fontaine–Mazur, logarithm-rank, reduction or local-height input remains an explicit condition on every downstream assertion. FAIL or unresolved candidate balls yield an open computation.
